through_line: On-device AI crossed an architectural threshold, not just a marketing one.
evidence_paragraph: oMLX introduces a tiered SSD KV cache that survives server restarts — local inference finally behaves like a real backend. OpenHuman stores a billion-token memory tree in Obsidian-readable markdown on your own disk, with TokenJuice compression to keep it usable. Needle strips out all feedforward layers so a 26M-parameter model compiles cleanly to the GEMMs already on mobile NPUs, targeting watches and glasses. Three builders, three different layers — inference, memory, model weight — each solving a concrete constraint that kept on-device AI feeling like a demo.
counter_signal: None of the three picks benchmarks on-device capability against a cloud equivalent on the same task, so the threshold crossed is size and persistence, not yet parity.
